surprise.title: 243 years ago today, two people flew free for the first time in history
surprise.body: On November 21, 1783, physicist Pilâtre de Rozier and an army officer, the marquis d'Arlandes, lifted off from the grounds of the Château de la Muette at the edge of Paris in a Montgolfier hot-air balloon with no tether at all. It was the first free flight by humans. They rose to about 900 metres, roughly 3,000 feet, drifted about nine kilometres across Paris, and came down 25 minutes later between the windmills on the Butte-aux-Cailles, outside the city walls. They had fuel left for four or five times that distance, but embers from their own fire kept scorching the balloon fabric, and the crew had to dab them out with sponges, with Pilâtre reportedly even using his coat. Only weeks earlier the Montgolfiers had tested the idea with a sheep, a duck, and a rooster in front of Louis XVI at Versailles. Tallahassee stays gray and mild today, about 62 to 65°F with rain chances near 50%, so it is an easy indoor Saturday. Twenty-two days until you sail on December 13.
